_meta.companion: data/telescopes/vista.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows elt.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; vista: title, telescope (machine-readable mirrors, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as 'vista.<param>'), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/vista/ (files reused from round 4 are byte-identical copies, marked in the cite). derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure (the caption quote is checked). INFERRED = a choice no source states. NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, approximately-equal sign, middle dot, plus-minus (to +/-), the degree sign and the ordinal sign used as a degree normalized; soft hyphens removed; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page and across consecutive page pairs (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF); HTML as tag-stripped text (tags to a space, tags removed) and raw source (UTF-8); .py as is.

explorer_preset.name: VISTA 4.1 m
explorer_preset.primaryNote: A Zerodur meniscus 4.10 m across (3.96 m clear) and 17 cm thick with a 1.20 m central hole: a hyperboloid with radius of curvature 8.094 m (f = 4.05 m, f/0.99 on 4.1 m), the most strongly curved mirror of this size. The 1.24 m secondary is undersized and is the stop, so each point of the field uses a 3.70 m circle of the primary.
explorer_preset.pupilNote: On the axis: the 3.70 m circle of the primary that the undersized secondary passes, less the 1.63 m baffle around the secondary and four 36 mm spider legs in two pairs, which leave the central barrel at opposite points on the altitude axis (horizontal here). The legs' angles (±60°) are a rough reading of photographs. Off the axis the 3.70 m circle shifts across the primary by up to 0.12 m.

conflicts: Pupil diameter: 3.70 m (S15, UM) vs 3.705 m (DERIVED, real-ray trace) vs 3.80 m (DERIVED paraxial image of M2, too large for the fast primary) vs the 3.95 m envelope (S15) vs the 3.96 m clear aperture (S15 Table 2) vs the 4.10 m mirror (headline).
Focal length with VIRCAM: 12.072 m (S15 Table 1, UM Sec. 5) vs 12.07 m and 17.0887 arcsec/mm = 12.0702 m (UM Sec. 6.2) vs '13 000 mm' (ESOVP).
VIRCAM focal ratio: f/3.25 quoted (S15, UM, ESOV, ESOVP) vs f/3.263 on 3.70 m and f/2.944 on 4.10 m (DERIVED).

4MOST field: 2.6 deg (UM19, DJ19, WS19) vs 2.5 deg (E4M, ESOI, H14, S15) vs 2.50 deg (DERIVED from the 535 mm focal diameter at 59.4 um/arcsec); fiber hexagon 4.1 deg^2 (ESOI) vs >4.2 deg^2 (UM19, WS19).

4MOST plate scale: 59.4 um/arcsec (UM19, EUSUB) vs ~60 um/arcsec (W26) vs ~63 um/arcsec (H14 concept: 12.995 m, f/3.51 on 3.70 m, which does not match H14's own f/3.32 = 59.55 um/arcsec on 3.70 m) vs '~60 mm/arcsec' (WS19 slide 16, a unit slip).

4MOST focal ratio: f/3.32 (H14; G14's 2012 baseline) vs f/3.20 (G14's alternative design, not built) vs f/3.311 on 3.70 m and f/2.988 on 4.10 m (DERIVED from 59.4 um/arcsec; round 4 quoted f/2.99 on 4.10 m).
Secondary: 'f/3 hyperboloid' (UM Sec. 5) vs R2 = 4018.9 mm, f/1.62 on 1.2415 m (DERIVED from S15 Table 2).
Unvignetted field: 2 deg (UM) vs the 1.65 deg VIRCAM field with cold-baffle vignetting from 0.69 deg to 1% at the corner (S15) vs a top ring sized for 4 deg (S15).
Site altitude: 2518 m (S15, ESOVP) vs 2500 m (UM Sec. 1) vs 2635.43 m (UM Table 2).

4MOST corrector: four lens groups with two counter-rotating prisms (EUSUB, WS19; built) vs the 2012 baseline with two rotating ADC doublets, six elements (G14) vs G14's alternative of four singlets with a laterally displaced ADC element.
notes: One focus, two instruments: VIRCAM was VISTA's only instrument from 2009 to March 2023; 4MOST took the same Cassegrain position (first light 2025), and ESO's 4MOST page (May 2026) calls 4MOST 'the only instrument installed at VISTA'. The mirrors serve both; each instrument brings a separate corrector, so the focal length and plate scale differ.

VISTA has no cold stop: the undersized secondary is the stop, so the pupil is smaller than the primary and moves across the primary with field angle (up to 0.12 m at 0.825 deg). The explorer draws the on-axis pupil.

Round 4 (data/round4/4most.md) used D = 4.10 m and derived f/2.99 for the 4MOST focus; on the 3.70 m entrance pupil the same 59.4 um/arcsec gives f/3.31, consistent with the baseline f/3.32. The spectrograph presets are not changed here.
The pupil frame follows S15 Sec. 5 (x along the altitude axis); with two symmetric pairs of legs the drawn pupil is the same seen from the sky or from the focus.
The 4MOST ETC's 8.452 m^2 and the explorer pupil (8.491 m^2) differ by 0.46%; with the legs as drawn, 8.452 m^2 corresponds to a 1.65 m obstruction.
